summary: A 1929 60-foot Aermotor LX-25 fire tower in Baxter County, Arkansas, kept by lookout keepers in the 1930s and 1940s, NHLR-registered in 2003 and listed as standing in 2023.

facts.design: 60-foot Aermotor LX-25 steel tower with a 7 by 7 metal cab; ladder-style steps between landings

staffing.status: keepers named in newspaper notices from 1934 to 1943; no later staffing found

events.note: Erected in 1929 on the Ozark National Forest; NHLR and the forest-lookout site agree on the year
C. W. Pemberton and family moved in as keeper for the coming year, per a January 5, 1934 Baxter Bulletin notice
Carba Pemberton, long-serving look-out man, resigned in July 1936 and planned to vacate within days
W. C. Norman described as keeping the tower; notices name him through 1943
Registered with the National Historic Lookout Register April 25, 2003; nominated by Michael A. Pfeiffer and Sue Foster
Listed as standing based on Google Earth imagery

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR gives coordinates 36.0845, -92.37017. An OpenStreetMap tower node (ID 359010507) sits about half a kilometre to the southwest at 36.07997, -92.37165. The NHLR registered coordinates are kept.
NHLR gives 1,234 ft (376 m). An OpenStreetMap node tags the elevation as 389 m. The NHLR figure is kept, since it is the registered value.

notes_for_editor: Build date and design agree across NHLR and the club page. Staffing comes only from newspaper notices copied by the club site (The Baxter Bulletin), so the keeper dates are secondhand and partial. Current access is unknown: no source says whether the tower is open or climbable, so no access key is set. The OpenStreetMap node is not cited in the story. The web search surfaced no independent 2020s source on condition. Suggest checking the Sylamore Ranger District for current status before publishing.
